title: Canada international Alphonso Davies suffers hamstring injury, out ‘several weeks’
content:
Canada international Alphonso Davies will miss “several weeks” of action due to a hamstring injury, his club Bayern Munich have confirmed.

The 25-year-old left-back was a second-half substitute in Bayern’s 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League semi-final on Wednesday and assisted Harry Kane’s stoppage-time equaliser.

However, the German club announced on Friday that “following an examination from Bayern’s medical unit”, it has been determined that the full-back injured his left hamstring in that game. They added Davies will “therefore be out of action for several weeks.”

Canada Soccer said it is in “close contact” with Davies and will remain in touch with Bayern’s medical team.

“Our focus is supporting his recovery and providing every available resource, including specialized soft tissue expertise, to give him the best possible pathway back to full fitness ahead of the FIFA World Cup,” a statement said.

Davies has made just 23 appearances this season, starting eight times in all competitions, after a number of injury issues in recent years.

The left-back tore the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee while on international duty in March of last year. Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen accused Canada Soccer of being “grossly negligent” in its handling of Davies’ injury. This season, he has missed games due to a hamstring injury and a muscle strain.

Canada are one of the hosts of this summer’s World Cup alongside the United States and Mexico. Davies is an integral part of Jesse Marsch’s Canada squad, having made 58 appearances for his nation and scoring 15 goals.

Canada were drawn into Group B and have group games against Bosnia & Herzegovina (June 12), Qatar (June 18) and Switzerland (June 24).

Before their World Cup kicks off, they face Uzbekistan (June 2) and the Republic of Ireland (June 6) in international friendlies.

Bayern secured the Bundesliga title last month and have two league games left to play: away to Wolfsburg on Saturday and then at home to Koln on May 16. Vincent Kompany’s side will face Stuttgart in the final of the DFB Pokal on May 23.

Analysis from Canadian soccer writer Joshua Kloke

Canada has suffered a rash of recent injuries ahead of their World Cup campaign but Davies’ injury is arguably their most concerning to date.

This is Davies’ fourth injury since March 2025. When Davies’ has suffered these recent injuries, there always appeared to be ample time for Canada’s star player to make a recovery. The unease around this injury feels different. Canadian players are set to report to Canada’s pre-World Cup training camp throughout mid-to-late May, meaning Davies might not be at full fitness at a time when Canada absolutely need him to be.

Canada’s training camp will feature typically intense training sessions led by head coach Jesse Marsch. The style of play Marsch wants his Canada team to unleash is relentless and high-tempo. Playing that way has allowed Canada to rise the FIFA rankings and develop a cohesive tactical approach. However this approach also places serious demands on players’ bodies. Any strain on players is amplified after a long season.

If Davies’ does return in time for Canada’s training camp, it’s still worth asking: will his recent injury limit how he can execute Marsch’s tactical and pressing demands? Or will Davies’ be rested to ensure he is fit for Canada’s World Cup opener on June 12, even if that means he misses Canada’s two pre-World Cup friendlies?

The pressure on Davies through this World Cup will be immense. He is Canada’s captain and the face of the program’s rise since 2019. Canada will need to balance his recent injury history with the need to ramp up his fitness to ensure he is at his most effective when it matters this summer.
